slides.headline: Slide 1
slides.body: How homeowners actually choose who to call

slides.headline: Slide 2
slides.body: They search first. Not from a truck sticker, not from a flyer — from their phone, when the problem happens.

slides.headline: Slide 3
slides.body: They look for a website before they look for a phone number. No site reads as no business.

slides.headline: Slide 4
slides.body: They check reviews next. A site with reviews built in does that work automatically.

slides.headline: Slide 5
slides.body: Only after that do they call — and usually just the first name that looked legitimate, not the best one.

slides.headline: Slide 6
slides.body: Being good at the trade was never the filter. Being findable was. We build the site that gets found.

caption1.variantA:
Nobody picks a contractor the way they used to.

Word of mouth still matters, but it isn't where the search starts anymore. It starts on a phone, usually right when the problem happens.

A homeowner searches, sees a few names, and narrows it down by whoever looks most legitimate in about ten seconds of scrolling.

That narrowing happens before anyone dials a number. It happens on whatever shows up when they search your name, or your trade, in your area.

If that's a real website with reviews and a clear way to call, you're in the running. If it's nothing, you're not.

Save this if it sounds familiar.

— Trevo
